selection: attention-compression layer classes; all three classes present in every forward
provenance: Shapes from config.json of the live checkpoint (hidden 4096, num_attention_heads 64, head_dim 512, num_key_value_heads 1, index_topk 512, sliding_window 128, compress_ratios) cross-checked against a rocprofv3 kernel trace on MI355X: 2666 split dispatches over 62 decode steps = 43/token, splitting 22/21 by VGPR class. Case counts are the compression partition: 21 C4 (compress_ratios==4), 20 C128 (==128), 2 ratio-0 (indices 0 and 1). NOT the routing partition (num_hash_layers=3 -> layers 0,1,2); layer 2 is hash-routed AND C4.
geometry_aggregation_key: grid(x,y,z) + workgroup(x,y,z) + VGPR + Accum_VGPR + SGPR + LDS + Scratch

observed_geometry.note: rocprofv3 Grid_Size is WORK-ITEMS, not workgroups. grid_split = (T, n_head_blocks, kv_splits).
observed_geometry.split: work-items (512,1,64) wg=512 -> 64 workgroups on 256 CUs; two VGPR classes 124 and 108, SGPR 64 both
observed_geometry.reduce: work-items (256,64,8) wg=256 -> 512 workgroups; single class, vgpr=16
observed_geometry.context_invariance: grid, VGPR and the 22:21 per-token class ratio are byte-identical at 128, 1024 and 16384 prefill tokens

physics: kv_splits is capped at _MAX_KV_SPLITS=64 while the kernel's own heuristic computes a device-fill target of 2 WG/CU = 512 workgroups. Measured on MI355X (ABBA, rocprofv3, GPU time of split+reduce): raising kv_splits 64 -> 256 costs +3.1% on split and +30.2% on reduce, net +10.1% worse at short K. The cap is real, not an oversight.
